findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key crashes on datetime fields
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key is copied verbatim from Paginator: it does `int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` on `getattr(item, self.key)`. When the audit log endpoint passes `order_by="-datetime"` (and AuditLogEntry.datetime is a DateTimeField), this fetches a `datetime` object and calls `math.floor(datetime)`, which raises `TypeError: a float is required`. The class should reuse DateTimePaginator's float-conversion logic (datetime.strftime('%s.%f') * multiplier) or be parameterized by key type. As written, any request with `optimized_pagination=true` against the audit log endpoint will 500 instead of returning data.

findings.title: enable_advanced_features kwarg is never forwarded to the paginator
findings.body: `self.paginate(..., enable_advanced_features=True)` passes `enable_advanced_features` as a keyword argument to Endpoint.paginate. Sentry's Endpoint.paginate does not forward arbitrary kwargs to the paginator constructor; it consumes named options (per_page, cursor, etc.) itself and uses **kwargs for response wrapping, not for paginator instantiation. The OptimizedCursorPaginator instance is therefore created with `enable_advanced_features=False` (its default), so the entire `if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0:` branch in paginator.py is unreachable. The user-facing `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter will appear to be honored while actually doing nothing — silently disabling the new code path. If forwarding is intended, paginate() must be changed to thread the kwarg into `paginator_cls(...)`; otherwise the call must construct the paginator directly.

findings.title: Negative-offset pagination bypasses cursor-based paging invariants
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[cursor.offset:stop]`). Cursor values come from the untrusted client via Cursor.from_string (cursors.py), so a caller can submit any negative integer and retrieve an arbitrary window into the queryset — e.g. `queryset[-1000000:stop]` is a valid SQL `OFFSET -1000000`. The comment "permissions are checked at the queryset level" is misleading: queryset-level filtering only restricts which organization is visible, not which row range is addressable. Combined with the fact that the cursor's `value` is also attacker-controlled, this exposes data the cursor protocol was specifically designed to forbid (the existing path in BasePaginator clamps to `max(0, offset)` for forward paging and validates offsets elsewhere). The new path must either reject negative offsets outright or bound them to a small, signed window (e.g. `max(-limit, cursor.offset)`).

findings.title: BasePaginator offset clamping is a behavior change mislabeled as an optimization
findings.body: BasePaginator previously did `queryset[offset:stop]` for both forward and prev pagination. The new code does `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` before slicing, which silently clamps negative offsets to 0 only for forward cursors. The inline comment calls this a "performance optimization for high-traffic scenarios" and asserts "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions", but this is actually a behavior change, not an optimization: any existing caller that produced a negative offset on a forward (is_prev=False) cursor — including cursors built by _build_prev_values whose is_prev is later overridden, or test fixtures, or cursors from older clients — will now incorrectly restart from the beginning of the dataset instead of returning the intended page. The docstring and commit message should describe it as a behavior change, and the change should be validated against every existing caller before merging.

findings.title: Comment claims an optimization that was not implemented
findings.body: The diff only adds the comments "Performance optimization: Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios" / "This enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets" above the unchanged line `self.offset = int(offset)`. No code in this file was modified — Cursor.__init__ already accepted any int via `int(offset)`, and the comments are misleading the reader into believing a new capability has been introduced in this file. Either remove the comments or move the actual negative-offset handling to a place where it has an effect.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator ships with no tests and duplicates BasePaginator
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator re-implements get_result() by copy-pasting the entire BasePaginator.get_result body rather than overriding only the new branch. This duplicates ~60 lines of pagination logic that already has subtle behavior (cursor-value skipping, prev-page boundary row handling, count_hits short-circuit, post_query_filter). Combined with the fact that no tests are added in this PR (the description is literally "Test 1") and the get_item_key method is incorrect for the only caller that uses it, the change is unverified and any future fix to BasePaginator.get_result will not be reflected in OptimizedCursorPaginator. Refactor to inherit the path (e.g. override a single `_resolve_slice(cursor, limit, extra)` hook in BasePaginator and call super), and add at minimum: (a) a datetime-key test confirming correct cursor values, (b) a test confirming negative offsets raise/clampt appropriately, and (c) a regression test that the audit log endpoint returns the same rows via DateTimePaginator and OptimizedCursorPaginator for ordinary requests.
